title: Chest Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a man with no significant past medical history who presents with acute chest pain that is pleuritic (worse with inspiration) and positional (relieved by leaning forward). He has no history of recent viral infection, making this likely idiopathic pericarditis. ECG shows diffuse ST elevation. Echocardiogram reveals a small pericardial effusion — no tamponade physiology. Troponin is negative, ruling out MI. First-line treatment: NSAIDs (ibuprofen/naproxen) PLUS colchicine — colchicine reduces symptoms and decreases rate of recurrent pericarditis. Add a PPI/H2 blocker for GI protection with high-dose NSAID therapy. Rest until symptoms resolve — activity can trigger recurrence. Pericardiocentesis is NOT indicated for small, asymptomatic effusions (only for moderate/large effusions > 2 cm or tamponade). Transesophageal echo is unnecessary — transthoracic echo is sufficient.
chief_complaint: Pleuritic chest pain, relieved by leaning forward

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Gauge how sick the patient may be.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Investigate for lung pathology. Pleuritic pain may have pulmonary origin.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Cardiac pathology often causes chest pain — must examine. Listen for pericardial friction rub.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Pain radiating to back — abdominal exam needed.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine
stacks.finding: Look for edema or pathology guiding workup.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: HEENT / Neck
stacks.finding: GERD or esophageal pathology could cause symptoms.

stacks.label: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: Check oxygenation if concerned about circulation.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: Good screening tool.

stacks.label: ECG, 12 lead
stacks.finding: ECG on every chest pain patient. Will show diffuse ST elevation in pericarditis (not territorial like MI).

stacks.label: Cardiac troponin I, serum
stacks.finding: Must rule out MI in chest pain. Negative in pericarditis.

stacks.label: Echocardiography (transthoracic)
stacks.finding: TTE shows small pericardial effusion. Transthoracic is sufficient — TEE is unnecessary and invasive.

stacks.label: TSH, serum
stacks.finding: Hypothyroidism can cause pericardial effusion.

stacks.label: Chest X-ray
stacks.finding: Rule out other causes of chest pain.

stacks.label: ANA, serum
stacks.finding: Autoimmune etiology is one cause of pericarditis.

stacks.label: Rheumatoid factor
stacks.finding: Autoimmune screening for pericarditis etiology.

stacks.label: BMP / CMP / LFTs
stacks.finding: Screening labs.

stacks.label: Echocardiography, transesophageal
stacks.finding: TTE is more than sufficient. TEE is invasive and unnecessary for small pericardial effusion — points lost for ordering.

stacks.label: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen / Naproxen / Aspirin)
stacks.finding: NSAIDs are treatment of choice for acute pericarditis.

stacks.label: Colchicine
stacks.finding: Added to NSAID therapy — reduces symptoms AND decreases rate of recurrent pericarditis. Well tolerated. Should be added for first-episode acute pericarditis.

stacks.label: PPI / H2 blocker (Omeprazole / Famotidine)
stacks.finding: High-dose NSAID therapy requires GI protection with PPI or H2 blocker.

stacks.label: Pericardiocentesis
stacks.finding: Only small effusion — will resolve on its own. Pericardiocentesis only for moderate/large effusions (>2 cm) or tamponade.

stacks.label: Advise patient, rest at home
stacks.finding: Activity may trigger recurrence. Rest until symptoms resolve.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Pericardial friction rub may be present (pathognomonic but not always). No muffled heart sounds (no tamponade).
physical_exam.respiratory: Pleuritic component — pain worse with inspiration.

decoys.label: Pericardiocentesis
decoys.reason_wrong: Small effusion resolves on its own. Pericardiocentesis is only indicated for moderate/large effusions (>2 cm) or cardiac tamponade.

decoys.label: Transesophageal echocardiography
decoys.reason_wrong: Invasive and unnecessary. TTE is sufficient to evaluate pericardial effusion. Ordering TEE loses points.

decoys.label: NSAIDs alone (without colchicine)
decoys.reason_wrong: Colchicine should be added to NSAID therapy for first-episode acute pericarditis — it reduces recurrence rate and improves symptom resolution.

decoys.label: Glucocorticoids as first-line
decoys.reason_wrong: Steroids are reserved for refractory pericarditis unresponsive to NSAIDs/colchicine, or autoimmune-associated pericarditis.

teach_me_steps.order: ECG in pericarditis: diffuse ST elevation
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Diffuse ST elevation (not territorial) + PR depression = pericarditis. Differentiate from MI (territorial ST elevation with reciprocal changes).
NSAIDs are cornerstone. Colchicine added reduces symptoms and decreases recurrent pericarditis rate. Add PPI for GI protection.

teach_me_steps.order: Avoid invasive procedures in small effusions
teach_me_steps.reasoning: Small pericardial effusion (<2 cm) resolves with medical management. Pericardiocentesis and TEE are unnecessary and lose points.
Physical activity can trigger recurrence. Advise home rest.

case_summary: Idiopathic acute pericarditis. Pleuritic chest pain + diffuse ST elevation + small effusion on echo. NSAIDs + colchicine + PPI. Avoid pericardiocentesis and TEE. ER then outpatient management with rest.
